# Prerequisite risks and unresolved claims

2026-11-01 UTC · **SOURCE-ONLY RESEARCH; NO EXECUTION PLAN**

These are scope/contract prerequisites, not an authorization or sequence of actions to implement, register, compile, load, or test anything. No earlier hold or C++ gate changes.

## 1. A real source/documentation discrepancy at the exact pin

The public comments for the error-code and error-text setters say a null **info handle** is accepted as a successful no-op. The inspected implementation instead returns `DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_INPUT_INVALID` when that handle is null. This is a narrow pinned comment/body disagreement, **not** a reproduced failure or a claim that non-null callback error propagation is broken. The minimum boundary can require a live non-null error carrier, but cannot claim that all documented nullable forms agree with source. [Public comments](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L2532-L2563), [actual setters](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/capi/v2/capi_v2_error.cpp#L23-L48).

Separately, a nearby strict-getter comment in the value source is stale: its actual ReadAs helper and public numeric-getter documentation both permit conversion. That is why this research uses the body rather than treating getter success as strict admission. This is not presented as an additional functional contradiction. [Actual conversion body](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/capi/v2/capi_v2_value.cpp#L55-L83), [public BIGINT getter contract](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L14583-L14599).

## 2. Binding/registration is a new authority and lifetime boundary

Connection registration is on the connection's **database**, visible to other connections according to transaction/commit visibility; it is not a private per-connection closure. The builder must originate from the same database. A per-request userdata pointer therefore needs an explicit identity/access/lifetime contract before exposing private owned input/output through a registered function. No registration/name/catalog mutation was performed or authorized by this research. [Pinned registration scope](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L13886-L13934).

Unresolved: whether the future surface is a permanent extension function, a separately authorized application registration, or another explicit request-binding mechanism; who can resolve a request; when it expires; what a prepared-call copy/rescan sees; whether counters describe a new reducer invocation or a retained immutable prior outcome. No global request registry, hidden ID, new predicate name, public ABI/IR identity, or reusable mutable request is selected.

## 3. Full typed carrier and strict admission remain unselected

Concrete SQL output types are required. Native primitive columns cover only explicitly homogeneous subsets; the whole domain needs an explicit tag-preserving carrier. UNION(BLOB/BOOLEAN/BIGINT/UBIGINT-word) and tagged STRUCT are feasible declaration-level candidates, not accepted mappings. Unresolved are member names/order, tag encoding, validity/inactive-payload invariants, SQL casts, external NULL rejection, NUL-free UTF-8 validation, exact f64-word admission/zero canonicalization, and preservation of bytewise extrema. SQL implicit casts, collation, UNION ordering, or native DOUBLE arithmetic cannot silently choose project semantics. [Concrete/nested types](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L8953-L9068), [nullable/cast-capable UNION background](https://duckdb.org/docs/2.0/sql/data_types/union).

No claim was verified that every finite binary64 interchange word round-trips through the host's DOUBLE constructor/vector path. Using an integer word avoids that particular conversion in a prospective carrier but does not prove an adapter. Native scalar/FP premises and deferred floating sum remain unchanged.

## 4. Arbitrary SQL ingress is materially larger than leaf egress

The inspected v2 table builder is an output-producing leaf with constant bind arguments; it does not expose an in-out child-row callback. A future top-level result consumer could own chunks and materialize a request outside callbacks, but that would add a new SQL/query/extraction boundary. It must establish the intended completed whole relation/cut, full tuple identity, raw transport order, strict validation of all supplied copies/fields, and independent accounting for host work. No query, extraction, completion certificate, temporal adapter, or replacement for blocked work is supplied here. [Constant argument representation](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb/main/capi_v2/capi_v2_function_internal.hpp#L121-L135), [actual leaf construction](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/capi/v2/capi_v2_func_table.cpp#L803-L835).

A native aggregate is larger again: mandatory combine, state aliases/lifetimes, final result offsets, host NULL filtering, cross-group error priority, full-tuple rather than measure deduplication, and exact raw-work traces need their own contract. Merely merging exact positive/negative totals does not prove disjoint contributors. No internal C++ API, custom spill architecture, or source-state export path is selected. [Pinned aggregate bridge](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/capi/v2/capi_v2_func_aggregate.cpp#L223-L375).

## 5. Error fidelity, streaming atomicity, interruption

The project's fixed structured error and counters are richer than a host error code/text pair. Their identity/ownership and a bounded non-payload-echoing translation are unresolved. Host text/error materialization can allocate and fail independently of the reducer's fixed error reserve; its source wrapper explicitly degrades error detail on allocation failure. Callback/opaque cleanup must not unwind or rely on an error slot to make a destructor succeed. [Host error allocation/return-code handling](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb/main/capi_v2/capi_v2_internal.hpp#L795-L837), [opaque destruction boundary](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L431-L440).

Reducer failure-before-output does not by itself provide atomic visibility across a streaming SQL consumer. Earlier caller-owned chunks can precede a later host/query failure. Whether the consumer accepts results only after stream completion, and how a cancelled/failed stream is distinguished, must be explicit. Likewise a connection interrupt declaration is not a demonstrated cancellation point inside a long native call or a latency bound. No runtime/interrupt/timeout experiment or new thread was started. [Stream ownership/errors](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L12148-L12225), [interrupt surface](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L2001-L2019).

## 6. Honest limits and status

- No accepted pushdown or partition claim is required for the minimum. Any later accepted filter must be equivalent to the engine predicate, and output projection must not redefine the source contribution set. [Pushdown responsibility](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L12807-L12854).
- Native logical counters/ceilings do not account for query execution, input materialization, bind ownership, host chunk copies, driver buffering, or physical allocation overhead. This research makes no host-memory/capacity/performance claim and does not infer that host vectors spill unrelated native owners.
- No old names/IR bytes/layouts/counters/limits have been changed. No lower-component completion, graph/temporal correctness, host compatibility, SQL agreement, old-surface compatibility, load/registration success, output-owner destruction, or production acceptance has been established.
- Exact-pin primary source was available and verified. **All empirical stages remain UNRUN**. Coordinator review and any future interface/implementation/empirical authority remain separate.
